title: Sell Mineral Rights in Canton, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Canton, PA | Bradford County
metaDescription: Canton, PA mineral owners in Bradford County: get a clear, no-pressure cash offer on your dry-gas Marcellus royalty interest.
heroLead: Canton sits along Route 6 in western Bradford County, in a stretch of the dry-gas Marcellus core that's been producing steadily for close to two decades.
intro: Canton is one of the working towns along the Route 6 corridor, surrounded by farmland that saw heavy Marcellus leasing during the county's early boom years. If your family holds minerals here, chances are the lease dates back to that period, and the royalty history since has run through the full arc of a typical Marcellus well: a strong initial few years, then a longer taper that's probably left your recent checks looking pretty different from what they were a decade ago.
We know arc because we've lived through it with our own family's interest. We'll walk you through exactly where your well sits in it before discussing any number.

sections.heading: Where a Canton-area well typically sits today
paragraphs: Given the timing of the early leasing rush in this part of Bradford County, most wells near Canton are well past their peak production years and settled into a slower, more predictable decline. That's not a bad thing for valuing your interest; it means we can price it against real, multi-year history instead of guessing at a new well's future performance.
This remains dry-gas Marcellus territory, with post-production deductions limited mostly to gathering and compression rather than the heavier liquids-processing costs seen in wet-gas counties.

sections.heading: The deduction issue, even without liquids
paragraphs: Even in a dry-gas county, Pennsylvania's Kilmer v. Elexco ruling allows operators to deduct gathering, compression, and transportation costs from your royalty. It's a smaller deduction than what wet-gas owners see, but it's still there, and it's still a source of real frustration for owners who signed a lease assuming gross proceeds meant gross proceeds.

sections.heading: What we check before making an offer
paragraphs: We confirm your chain of title through the Bradford County Recorder of Deeds, verify your decimal interest, and review recent statements so any number reflects your actual, current production.

faqs.question: My royalty checks are much smaller now than they were years ago. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: Yes, typically. Marcellus wells produce their strongest volumes in the first few years before settling into a longer, slower decline, which shows directly in your royalty.

faqs.question: Do dry-gas wells still have post-production deductions?
faqs.answer: Yes, generally for gathering and compression, though usually smaller than the liquids-processing deductions seen in wet-gas counties.

faqs.question: Is a well nearly two decades into production still worth selling?
faqs.answer: Often yes, since the long production history lets us value it with real confidence rather than a projection.
